Bitget Hack Update: Why Loss Estimate Rise to $387.5M? Bitget Hack Update: When Will Withdrawals Resume After $387M Hit? Sakshi Jain Published: September 26, 2026 Last Updated: 26 Sep 2026 Share: TWITTER Linkedin FACEBOOK Bitget Hack Update 2026: What Happened? When Will Withdrawals Restart? Bitget Exchange found and fixed the bug behind its September 24 crypto hack . The exchange will bring back withdrawals in steps, starting September 28. Bitget also raised its loss estimate to about $387.5 million. The old number was $351.6 million. The new number counts Zcash and TRON assets that were missed at first. At a Glance The exchange spotted the hack on September 24, 2026
Withdrawals restart in steps from September 28
Mandiant and SlowMist are helping with the probe
Bitget started a bounty to help recover funds
Bitget Hack Update: Fixes Vulnerability After September 24 Security Incident
Bitget's security incident team caught bad transfers from a few hot wallets on September 24. This happened at about 18:31 UTC. The team acted fast. It turned on its emergency plan and began digging in. Most of the funds stayed safe. Cold wallets were not touched.
Since then, the team has found how the breach happened. They found the exact bug the attackers used. The bug is now fixed. The exchange also says the exploit is over. No more funds can be taken. Bitget exchange has not shared every detail yet. It says the probe is still open.
At first, it was about $351.6 million that was hit. New checks raised that number to $387.5 million. This does not mean a new hack took place. The higher number just adds in assets on two chains: Zcash and TRON. Those were missed the first time.
The hack touched many chains. This includes Ethereum and other EVM chains, plus XRP, Zcash, and TRON.
XRP, ETH, USDT, ZEC, USDC, USDT0, XAUt, BNB, AVAX, TRX
This is the part users care about most. The crypto exchnage paused withdrawals as a safety step. It says this was not because user funds were at risk. Withdrawals will come back in stages. Big coins go first.
Timeline: Bitget Withdrawal Restoration Schedule
Sept 28, 8:00 UTC: BTC withdrawals return
Sept 29, 8:00 UTC: ETH withdrawals return (Ethereum, BSC, Arbitrum, Base, Optimism)
Sept 30, 8:00 UTC: USDT withdrawals return (Ethereum, BSC, Solana, Tron)
Oct 2, 8:00 UTC: Other coins, cash, and P2P return
These times equal 4:00 PM Beijing time on each date. The trading and deposits work fine right now.
Mandiant and SlowMist are still on the case. They work with Bitget's own team. The team has traced the stolen funds. They found the wallets the hackers used. This spans EVM chains, XRP Ledger , Zcash, and TRON. Police are also involved now.
The loss number could shift again. More checks may turn up more facts. But it still says the hack is contained. No new theft has occurred since.
It wants help getting the stolen funds back. So it made a bounty plan. Anyone can join: exchanges, security experts, or everyday sleuths. Here's how it works:
5% of any frozen funds go to the person who helped freeze them
5% of any recovered funds go to the person who helped recover them
The help must be voluntary, not court-ordered
The exchange picks who gets paid and how much
Bybit Lazarus Bounty tool will help run this effort
Stablecoin firms have also jumped in. CoinDesk reports that Circle and Tether froze one wallet tied to the crypto hack. That move locked up 218,023 USDT and 99,990 USDC. Together, that's about $318,000. Circle acted first, at 5:00 AM UTC on September 25. Tether followed soon after. MistTrack confirmed both moves.
This is a small piece of the total loss. MistTrack says other hacker wallets still hold over 63,000 ETH. Stablecoin firms can't freeze ETH the same way.
Binance founder Changpeng "CZ" Zhao publicly responded to the Bitget hack, calling it a tough day for the exchange. He said he expects Binance, the BNB Chain ecosystem, and the wider crypto community to help out however they can. CZ also reminded users to put safety first during the incident, closing his post with Binance's familiar "Stay SAFU" message.
Other exchange leaders echoed similar support. Bybit CEO Ben Zhou, Binance Co-CEO Richard Teng, MEXC CEO Vugar Usi, and CoinDCX co-founder Sumit Gupta all publicly offered assistance the same day, signaling a broader industry response to the hack beyond Bitget's own team.
You don't need to do anything before withdrawals return
Watch the Bitget app for withdrawal updates
Bitget Wallet is separate and was not affected by this hack
The crypto exchange fixed the bug from its September 24 hack. It will bring back withdrawals starting September 28. The loss estimate now stands near $387.5 million, mostly due to newly found Zcash and TRON funds.
Mandiant and SlowMist keep helping with the probe. Bitget's bounty plan and the Circle/Tether freeze mark early wins in getting funds back. Full recovery is still not certain.

Crime How AI Helped Chainalysis Investigators Trace the $387 Million North Korea Stole from Bitget October 1, 2026 | Chainalysis Team Summary Since $387 million was stolen from Bitget on September 24, Chainalysis investigators have been working with the exchange and law enforcement partners to trace the stolen funds across multiple blockchains and protocols.
Our team quickly built custom tooling and automation for the investigation using our in-house AI. This helped investigators reduce tracing time, connect seemingly fragmented on-chain activity, and uncover new links across the investigation.
The DPRK-attributed attack pushes the total value of crypto stolen by North Korea actors in 2026 past $1 billion. In the coming weeks, our team will continue to monitor the stolen funds, label linked addresses, and share intelligence with counterparts.
When Chainalysis began tracing the $387 million stolen from Bitget last week, we knew the actors behind the exploit would move quickly. So our investigators leveraged in-house AI to create custom automations that matched their speed.
In a round-the-clock war room, our Customer Outcomes team kept Bitget and law enforcement partners updated with the latest insights Chainalysis derived while following the money. We boosted our efforts by building custom automation tools to move fast, cutting out manual tracing of complex transactions across multiple blockchains and reconciling activity at each step. We estimate that more than 20 hours of manual bridge reconciliation was compressed to under 10 minutes.
As can be seen in the graph below, which shows a portion of the transfers, hundreds of transfers have been carried out since the attack began. The funds were transferred between different networks, such as from Ethereum to Bitcoin.
Scaling cross-chain analysis with custom tooling
This wasn’t simply an AI-assisted tool to help our investigators build graphs. Our agentic platform gives our experts the ability to interrogate Chainalysis and other data sources to quickly develop custom solutions tailored to the specific investigation.
Importantly, this did not replace our investigative expertise. Rather, it accelerated it. Our investigators still defined the logic, reviewed the outputs, and directed the investigation.
The ability to quickly identify and understand illicit activity is increasingly important as DPRK and other threat actors use sophisticated automation to move and obscure stolen funds. Investigators must keep pace with these tactics while applying the judgment and expertise needed to make sense of complex on-chain activity.
That makes speed a critical part of the investigative process. Within minutes of identification, labels flagging stolen funds were live in our data platform, giving compliance teams and law enforcement the data they needed to act.
In the first three hours after the exploit, $387 million left Bitget across 23 transfers, landing on four chains: Ethereum (49.7%), XRP (40.8%), Zcash (7.6%), and Tron (1.8%), as shown below. From there, we identified distinct laundering mechanisms used by the threat actors, from cross-chain liquidity and messaging protocols to instant swaps. We also identified links to laundering services.
Our investigators’ ability to reconstruct the movements of funds across pathways using the custom tooling was particularly important for the stolen XRP. Rather than sending the XRP to an exchange, the attackers pushed it through a cross-chain liquidity protocol and took Bitcoin out the other side.
In simple terms, such protocols let someone deposit one asset on one chain and receive a different asset on another without an account or intermediary connecting the two sides. But each swap still leaves an on-chain record.
Our investigators matched deposits to their corresponding payouts, bridging the gap between blockchains and extending the trail.

This network has been growing in scope for years , posing a greater risk to corporations duped into hiring the agents, as well as providing Pyongyang with a steady flow of cash. In this instance, the DPRK workers and their facilitators leveraged Russian nationals to convert the crypto into cash.

Bitget Loses USD 351.6 Million in Hot Wallet Breach in Likely North Korea Attack | TRM Labs Insights September 25, 2026 Bitget Loses USD 351.6 Million in Hot Wallet Breach in Likely North Korea Attack TRM Team On September 24, 2026, attackers moved an estimated USD 351.6 million out of Bitget’s hot and warm wallets across Ethereum, the XRP Ledger, Arbitrum, Avalanche, Optimism, BNB Chain, and Base. Bitget detected the unauthorized transfers at 18:31 UTC, paused withdrawals, and said the loss falls within its User Protection Fund. It is the largest crypto theft of 2026 by value so far. Key takeaways Attackers moved an estimated USD 351.6 million from Bitget’s hot and warm wallets on September 24, 2026. Bitget says they compromised a backend system, manipulated the transaction data shown to its authorization process, and caused it to approve the transfers. The exchange says its private keys were not stolen.
Early estimates of USD 170–190 million covered the EVM chains. TRM data shows about USD 158 million also left through the XRP Ledger, bringing the observed outflows close to Bitget’s reported loss.
The stolen ETH and XRP were quickly split among new wallets, many holding round amounts of roughly 10,000 ETH or 20 million XRP. By the morning of September 25, most of those funds had not moved again.
Bitget paused withdrawals and says its USD 464 million User Protection Fund covers the loss. It says cold wallets were unaffected.
Bitget’s CEO has described North Korean involvement as “very likely,” though TRM has not definitively attributed the attack. Multiple on-chain links to previously identified North Korean thefts, including Bybit and AFX Bridge, point toward North Korean involvement. Those links run through a laundering network TRM has not observed working with any other group, though another actor carrying out the theft remains technically possible.
Exchanges use hot and warm wallets to process withdrawals while keeping most customer assets in cold storage. Transfers from those wallets still require approval before they are signed. Bitget CEO Gracy Chen said an attacker gained access to a backend system connected to its wallet infrastructure, spoofed transaction data, and triggered that approval process. Bitget says its private keys were not compromised and its cold wallets were unaffected.
The failure resembles the February 2025 Bybit theft in one respect: the attacker manipulated what the people or systems authorizing a transfer saw. At Bybit, that led signers to approve a transfer from a cold wallet. At Bitget, according to the exchange, it caused its withdrawal controls to authorize transfers from hot and warm wallets. Neither account depends on stolen private keys.
Early onchain estimates put the loss at USD 170–190 million because they covered Ethereum and other EVM chains. Bitget reported a loss of USD 351.6 million. TRM data shows approximately USD 158 million in XRP and USD 7 million in TRX also leaving Bitget wallets, bringing the observed outflows close to the exchange’s figure.
The proceeds were split into round-number wallets within hours
On Ethereum, much of the stolen value passed through 0x770b10b273fC44Fe9197D6bF20F145c2e98463Ee, which also received funds on Arbitrum, Avalanche, Base, BNB Chain, and Optimism. A second wallet, 0xa6dd3f218b65e32ccc37be30f74884133c655545, distributed its balance to newly created wallets over roughly two hours on the evening of September 24. Most received about 10,000 ETH each. Together with wallets funded directly from the first address, eight wallets received most of the stolen ETH. None had sent funds onward as of the morning of September 25.
The XRP followed a similar pattern. Funds leaving Bitget passed through smaller relay accounts before arriving in separate accounts holding round amounts of 20 million XRP. Most of that XRP also remained in place as of the morning of September 25.

Skip to main The Democratic People's Republic of Korea ( North Korea ) continues to improve its tactics to infiltrate western companies with thousands of state-controlled remote "IT Workers" ( ITW s) while avoiding detection. ITWs are increasingly using facilitators to counter improved private sector detections and law enforcement actions. The FBI has observed North Korean ITWs use stolen identities, extort victims, and use threats of physical violence to demand payments. ITWs fund North Korea's government, including its nuclear weapons and other military programs, and pose a significant national security and intellectual property theft insider threat. The FBI is updating its previous guidance to the public and private sector on techniques and recommendations to identify and avoid this threat. This includes tips to protect yourself and your business, as well as a larger description of how the threat has recently evolved. The general public needs to be aware that North Korean ITWs increasingly rely on the help of witting and unwitting Americans to acquire jobs in the United States, and they strategically target those under financial stress. ITWs are paying Americans for an expanding range of services to hide their own involvement in the scheme, including asking some to appear on camera, participate in job interviews or meetings, verify fraudulent identities, provide access to personal social media or professional networking accounts, ship packages, complete urinalysis tests or fingerprint submissions, or keep employment-related devices connected to the Internet from personal residences. These actions are illegal, and participating in them puts individuals at risk of law enforcement scrutiny. U.S. companies should recognize the scale, persistence, and rapid evolution of the North Korean ITW threat means ITWs cannot be identified reliably with a single indicator. Mirroring cybersecurity concepts, detection requires an "identity in depth" approach for effective defense, consisting of multiple layered access controls and detections throughout the employment lifecycle to find, interdict, and remove ITWs regardless of North Korean tactical innovations. Tips to Protect Yourself as an Individual For the public , the FBI provides the following information and general recommendations to prevent falling victim to the North Korean ITW scheme. Be aware North Korean ITWs post fake job openings on well-known job boards often as freelance gigs with simple requests such as interviewing on someone's behalf or receiving and hosting laptops in your home.
ITWs routinely invent elaborate stories, create fake companies, and produce official documentation to lend credibility to their requests. Common ITW backstories include claiming to be Chinese or East Asian nationals in need of a temporary U.S. presence or claiming to be Eastern Europeans displaced by the ongoing Russia-Ukraine war.
Reject any request to provide personal information, personal details, financial information, or personal account logins in exchange for payment.
Be aware ITWs have used threats of violence and other acts of intimidation to try to compel Americans to continue illicit activities. If you or someone you know receives a threat to life or is concerned about physical safety, call 911.

sources.text: Advertisement By&nbsp Angela Barnes Published on 30 October 2026 - 6:05 GMT+1 • Updated 8:20 Share Comments Add Euronews on Google Share Facebook Twitter Flipboard Send Reddit Linkedin Messenger Telegram VK Bluesky Threads Whatsapp Cryptocurrency platform Binance said on Thursday it had fallen victim to a major hack that hit around $6.3 billion (€5.5bn) in funds, with about half that amount frozen to prevent a massive theft. The company - the world's largest crypto exchange by daily trading volumes - posted a series of sometimes contradictory messages on X, insisting that "user funds are completely safe" but also saying it would "cover all losses". ADVERTISEMENT ADVERTISEMENT Binance later said on its X account for Latin America that "the total estimated impact is around $6.3bn (€5.5bn)". "We have worked with blockchain partners to freeze the affected assets, with ~ $3bn (€2.6bn) frozen on-chain so far," it added. That would be more than four times the amount involved in what had been the biggest-ever cyberattack of its kind to date: $1.5bn (€1.3bn) taken in February 2025 from the Bybit platform. The Bybit heist was attributed at the time to a group of hackers affiliated with North Korea called TraderTraitor. Blockchain investigation firm TRM Labs said on Thursday it had "high confidence" that the Binance hack was also orchestrated by TraderTraitor, citing "robust on and off-chain intelligence". "Several features of this attack match earlier North Korea-linked heists," TRM said. TraderTraitor is believed to be part of Lazarus Group - which gained notoriety in 2014 when it was accused of hacking into Sony Pictures as revenge for "The Interview", a film that mocked North Korean leader Kim Jong Un. Fund freeze At about 0030 GMT (0230 CEST) on Friday, Binance said all deposits and withdrawals had been "temporarily suspended while our team conducts security checks, freezes funds and works with law enforcement". "This figure may continue to increase as our teams work closely with law enforcement, issuers, blockchain intelligence firms and industry partners to trace and freeze additional assets," the company said. The company's statement on X said an initial investigation suggested the hack involved a compromised laptop belonging to a "DevOps engineer", allowing the unauthorised party to access a "service container" and execute unauthorised withdrawal transactions. "We have found no evidence of any private key leaks from wallets," Binance said, promising to share a detailed technical analysis once investigations were complete. Paolo Ardoino, the boss of Tether - a company that issues a cryptocurrency known as USDT - said his firm had frozen about $1.6bn (€1.4bn) "related to a potential Binance exchange hack". Jeremy Allaire, who runs cryptocurrency platform Circle, said his company had frozen more than $800m (€696m) in USDC. USDT and USDC are both "stablecoins", or digital currencies whose value is linked to a traditional currency, the US dollar. The US Department of Justice and the FBI did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Crypto prices tumble For several hours before Binance confirmed the attack, industry observers said hackers had managed to reach the platform. The prices of most major cryptocurrencies fell on news of the cyberattack, with the exception of stablecoins, which by definition can only fluctuate within tight margins. At about 0400 GMT (0600 CEST), bitcoin and Ethereum were down 0.8%, recovering after plunges of nearly 5% and nearly 6%, respectively. BNB, Binance's native cryptocurrency, was up 2.7% after tumbling nearly 10%. The attack on Binance comes as many observers express concerns that the ever-expanding capabilities of artificial intelligence (AI) models could compromise cryptography and IT security protocols. On Ethereum, the attacker used an EIP-7702 delegation to turn a Binance hot wallet into a sweeper it controlled, with 50 pre-signed authorizations prepared in advance. In the same window, Binance wallets on the other nine chains sent funds to the attacker through ordinary signed transfers. In TRM's assessment, this points to a compromise of Binance's hot wallet signing infrastructure.

AI-powered investigations company TRM Labs said in a report that several elements of the Binance attack resemble earlier North Korean-linked incidents, including the Bybit hack.
The lab's global head of policy Ari Redbord told the BBC the Binance hack is a "watershed moment" that is unlike anything the industry has seen.
The attacker still holds an enormous sum of stolen assets, meaning efforts to trace and recover the funds are far from over, Redbord added.
Binance, which was founded in China in 2017, allows users to trade digital assets and is estimated to have more than 300 million registered users worldwide.
The company said in 2024 that it has more than $160bn in assets under its custody.

Seoul fears being left out as US reaches out to North Korea Skip to content
South Korea has been facing pressure both from North Korea and from its ally, the United States Image: Evan Vucci/AP Photo/picture alliance Advertisement South Korea 's relationship with the North, always strained, seems to be going through a particularly hostile patch in recent weeks.
Last month, Seoul accused North Korea of planting a mine on the southern side of the heavily fortified border. The device exploded, injuring three South Korean soldiers . Pyongyang refused to apologize and insisted this was a false-flag incident designed to tarnish the isolated nation. The North Korean regime has since conducted multiple weapons tests , held its first-ever exhibition of military drones attended by Kim Jong Un, brought up self-propelled artillery units to the border and started preparing loudspeaker systems that will blast propaganda into the South.
On Thursday, North Korea also fired around 10 short-range ballistic missiles towards the Sea of Japan just before a scheduled visit to South Korea by German Chancellor Friedrich Merz .
On top of South Korea's issues with its archrival, however, many in Seoul are growing increasingly wary of their most important ally, the United States. South Korean politicians are worried that the US could push for a diplomatic breakthrough with North Korea to the point of ignoring South Korea's security , or even leave it exposed to Pyongyang's nuclear arsenal.
Who gets a voice on South Korea's future?
US President Donald Trump famously claimed he and Kim Jong Un "fell in love" during Trump's first term. More recently, Trump has indicated he would like to resume talks and there have been suggestions that a meeting could take place on November 18 in the Chinese city of Shenzhen, where Trump is expected to attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit.
The North Korean side has made no official response to Washington's hints, although South Korea's National Intelligence Service informed a closed-door meeting of Seoul's intelligence committee on Thursday that Kim Jong Un discussed the possibility of meeting Trump when he met with senior members of China's politburo in Dandong on Saturday.
Seoul's fears were also fueled by the US proposing three-way talks with Russia and China on the fate of Ukraine, without inviting a representative of Kyiv to attend. The worry in Seoul is that President Donald Trump may similarly bypass Seoul to discuss the future of the Korean Peninsula with China and North Korea.
Washington-Seoul relationship shaken by tariffs, funding disputes
"Right now, there is a problem of trust between the two governments," said Kim Sang-woo, a former politician with the left-leaning South Korean Congress for New Politics and now a member of the board of the Kim Dae-jung Peace Foundation.
A security and trade relationship that was previously considered secure has been rocked by tariffs, trade restrictions and demands from Washington that the South pay more for the US troops stationed in the country, Kim told DW.

Bitget $387M Hack AI Tracing Speeds Blockchain Forensics Skip to content Bitget’s $387M hack AI tracing cuts 20 hours to 10 minutes By Francesco Antonio Russo 3 October 2026, 14:16 4 min read In AI Bitget $387M Hack AI Tracing Speeds Blockchain Forensics Share X Telegram WhatsApp LinkedIn Email Chainalysis says it used in-house artificial intelligence to cut a bridge reconciliation task that would normally take investigators more than 20 hours down to under 10 minutes while tracing the $387 million drained from crypto exchange Bitget. The breakdown comes from a Chainalysis report dated Oct. 1, as crypto.news reported. The blockchain analytics firm said its investigators built custom automation specifically for the case after Bitget detected unauthorized transfers on Sept. 24, and the tool helped connect fragmented transaction trails that would otherwise look unrelated when viewed on separate networks. Summary Key takeaways Chainalysis says its AI shrank a 20-hour bridge-matching task to under 10 minutes during the Bitget probe.
Roughly $387 million left Bitget across Ethereum, XRP, Zcash and Tron in 23 transfers.
Chainalysis links the theft to North Korean actors, whose 2026 crypto thefts now top $1 billion.
Circle and Tether froze about $318,000 in linked USDC and USDT by Sept. 26.
How AI Tracing Accelerated the Bitget Hack Investigation
Chainalysis investigators set the matching logic themselves, then let the AI handle the repetitive cross-chain legwork of pairing deposits on one network with payouts on another. “Our investigators still defined the logic, reviewed the outputs, and directed the investigation,” the firm said in its report. Newly flagged addresses tied to the stolen funds received labels within minutes, feeding directly into the compliance data platform used by exchanges and law enforcement partners.
Inside the $387 Million Theft Across Four Blockchains
Within the attack’s first three hours, Chainalysis tracked 23 separate transfers that drained roughly $387 million from Bitget. According to its analysis, 49.7% went to Ethereum, 40.8% to XRP, 7.6% to Zcash and 1.8% to Tron.
Investigators traced the stolen XRP through a cross-chain liquidity protocol that paid out Bitcoin rather than routing the tokens straight to an exchange, with tens of millions of dollars passing through that route over roughly a day and a half. From there, the funds moved through several more protocols to attacker-controlled Bitcoin addresses that Chainalysis said it continues to monitor.
Bitget’s own investigation traced the breach to a vulnerability in a third-party security product that let attackers obtain credentials and forge withdrawal commands. Mandiant and SlowMist assisted with the forensic work. According to Chainalysis, North Korean actors were behind the attack, pushing the group’s cumulative 2026 crypto theft past $1 billion, whereas Bitget CEO Gracy Chen initially pointed only to IP patterns and VPN infrastructure resembling known North Korean tactics, stopping short of a definitive attribution.
Bitget’s Response: Detection, Rewards and Restored Withdrawals
According to Bitget, its systems detected unauthorized transfers at 18:31 UTC on Sept. 24 originating from segments of its hot and warm wallet infrastructure. The exchange subsequently revised its estimated losses upward, moving from $351.6 million to $387.5 million once further Zcash and Tron transfers were accounted for.
To claw back funds, Bitget offered separate 5% rewards for information leading to frozen assets and for successful recovery. Circle and Tether froze about $318,000 in linked USDC and USDT by Sept. 26. In its update on Sept. 30, Bitget verified that withdrawal functions had come back online in phases — Bitcoin on Sept. 28, followed by Ether on Sept. 29 and USDT on Sept. 30 — while reiterating that user funds remained untouched and that more than $300 million had already flowed back into its Protection Fund.

Robert Cammarano (left) entering the South Australian Supreme Court. ( ABC News: Eva Blandis )
The labour hire company at the centre of a controversy surrounding alleged bikie threats is still awaiting a payment of about $2 million from the lead contractor of the South Australian government's Torrens to Darlington project, a court has heard.
The company, Career Boss Australia, had its contract to supply workers on the $15.4 billion South Road upgrade suspended on October 18 after it was revealed in the media it was the subject of a civil dispute in the Supreme Court.
That claim, lodged by businessman Robert Cammarano, alleges that bikie Jamie Brown "coerced the transfer" of shares in the company, without Mr Cammarano's authority, by making "express threats of physical harm".
Mr Cammarano's claim also alleges other shareholders were threatened to transfer their shares.
Brown is yet to file a defence but has reportedly told 7News he had "never threatened any shareholder and allegations to the contrary are simply false".
At a hearing on Friday, barrister Tim Kentish, for Mr Cammarano, sought a freeze on a bank account connected to Career Boss Australia.
He said the company was still expecting a payment "around the $2 million mark" from John Holland, the lead contractor on the Torrens to Darlington project.
"That was the vast bulk of the revenue that's been coming in to this company — there's not a lot else," Mr Kentish said of the South Road contract.
"There's a final payment coming in, that's due to come in from John Holland for work performed, they pay in arrears, in the order of a couple million dollars."
The Torrens to Darlington project is expected to cost about $15 billion and is the most expensive infrastructure project ever carried out in South Australia. ( Supplied: SA Government )
Subpoena sought for recording of meeting
Mr Kentish also asked for the judge to subpoena a recording he alleges police have obtained of a meeting between "various parties" where the alleged "expropriation of the shares" was discussed.
A Crown solicitor, appearing on behalf of the acting commissioner of SA Police, asked this request to be adjourned so police could consider the "scope of the orders and whether or not to agree".
Associate Justice Graham Dart agreed to defer consideration of the subpoena request.
He also ordered a temporary freeze on the bank account connected to Career Boss Australia.
Outside court, Mr Cammarano said "we had a good win today" but did not comment further.
The matter was adjourned until November 16.
'No payments being made', govt says
The case surrounding Career Boss Australia and involvement in South Australia's largest-ever infrastructure project has triggered an escalating political crisis for the Malinauskas government.
A representative of Mr Cammarano notified Transport Minister Joe Szakacs's chief of staff and Child Protection Minister Alice Rolls about the allegations at a meeting on September 11.
Mr Szakacs's office passed on the claims to the South Road project team, which investigated the claims.

sections.heading: North Korean actors stole $6.75 billion from Bitget and Binance in 2026
paragraphs: North Korean actors stole $387.5 million from Bitget and $6.36 billion from Binance during two hacks in 2026. The Bitget theft occurred on September 24, 2026, while the Binance breach took place on October 29, 2026. TRM Labs attributes the Binance hack with high confidence to the TraderTraitor group, which is linked to North Korea’s Lazarus Group. Actors linked to the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea also took the $387.5 million from Bitget, according to source S4. This total exceeds $1 billion in cryptocurrency stolen by North Korean actors in 2026. These state-run programs provide funds for weapons programs, while the losses are borne by private users, exchanges and market stability.

Bitget initially estimated its September 24 loss at $351.6 million, but later revised the figure to $387.5 million to include Zcash and TRON assets. The attackers used a backend system that spoofed transaction data, which allowed unauthorized approvals without compromising private keys. Stolen funds were traced to wallets on the XRP Ledger, Zcash, TRON and Ethereum. Bitget paused withdrawals after the incident and began restoring them in stages starting September 28 for BTC and September 29 for ETH. Mandiant and SlowMist are assisting the exchange with the investigation. The company launched a bounty program that pays 5% of any frozen or recovered funds to individuals who help.

Binance lost an estimated $6.36 billion on October 29, 2026, in the largest crypto heist on record. This breach surpassed the $1.5 billion Bybit hack from February 2025. An attacker moved the funds out of Binance wallets on ten blockchains within 20 minutes starting at 20:05 UTC. Initial investigations point to a compromised laptop belonging to a DevOps engineer, which gave the attacker access to a service container. Binance temporarily suspended all withdrawals and deposits after the hack. The exchange stated it will cover all hacking losses, although it also posted messages on X stating that user funds are completely safe.

Tether, Circle, Ripple and World Liberty Financial froze $2.67 billion in stablecoins following the Binance breach. Arbitrum’s Security Council froze 8,426 ETH and 74.6 million ARB, which totals approximately $2.7 billion. Despite these freezes, the attacker controlled 420,000 ETH and 18,270 BTC, valued at $2.4 billion, in wallets beyond the reach of any issuer. Binance is working with law-enforcement agencies, token issuers and blockchain-intelligence firms to trace the remaining assets. The exchange has not provided an update on the remaining $3.3 billion of assets. Approximately $3 billion of the stolen assets have been frozen on-chain, according to sources S11 and S12.

Market participants suffered price drops in the hours after the Binance breach was announced. Bitcoin fell more than 4% according to source S2, while source S12 reported it dropped more than 3% to a six-week low. Ethereum fell more than 3% to a two-month low during the same period. Victims of these thefts include exchange users and broader crypto-market participants. Bitget users are covered by its User Protection Fund, but Binance users may be at risk despite claims that funds are safe. The FBI reports that North Korean IT workers use stolen identities and extortion to fund the regime’s nuclear and missile programs.

sections.heading: Bitget hack on 24 September 2026 exploited software bug, paused withdrawals and opened bounty
paragraphs: On 24 September 2026 Bitget suffered a hack that resulted in the theft of crypto assets, according to Bitget (C1). The breach exploited a software bug in a backend system that spoofed transaction data, allowing unauthorized approvals without the private keys being compromised (C38, C72). Bitget said the exploit has been fixed and is no longer active (C3, C40). The company also reported that the bug was addressed across its infrastructure, preventing further unauthorized transactions (C3). The hack therefore represents a breach of Bitget’s internal controls rather than a compromise of user private keys (C38).

Bitget initially reported a loss of $351.6 million, but later revised the figure to $387.5 million to include Zcash and TRON assets that were missed in the first count (C2). The exchange disclosed that 49.7 % of the stolen value moved on Ethereum, 40.8 % on the XRP Ledger, 7.6 % on Zcash and 1.8 % on TRON (C71). Two primary theft wallets – 0x770b10b273fC44Fe9197D6bF20F145c2e98463Ee and 0xa6dd3f218b65e32ccc37be30f74884133c655545 – split the stolen ETH into round‑number wallets of roughly 10,000 ETH each and created similarly sized XRP wallets (C29, C73, C56). TRM Labs noted on‑chain links between the Bitget theft and earlier North Korean‑attributed attacks, suggesting the same state‑backed actors were involved (C30). The attackers also used a cross‑chain liquidity protocol for XRP instead of sending it to an exchange (C59, C90).

Bitget paused all withdrawals immediately after the hack and began restoring them in stages, the exchange said (C4, C8). Bitcoin withdrawals resumed on 28 September 2026, followed by Ethereum and related chains on 29 September, USDT on 30 September, and other assets on 2 October (C4). Bitget asserted that the breach is contained and no new thefts have occurred since the 24 September incident (C8). The staged restart was communicated to users through official channels, indicating the platform’s effort to balance security with service continuity (C4). During the pause, the exchange worked with external firms to investigate the incident (C5).

Bitget launched a bounty program that pays 5 % of any frozen funds and 5 % of any recovered funds to individuals who help freeze or recover them, the exchange announced (C6). The program is intended to incentivize third‑party assistance in tracking and retrieving the stolen assets (C6). Mandiant and SlowMist are assisting Bitget with the investigation, providing technical expertise and threat‑intel support (C5). The bounty terms were disclosed in Bitget’s public statement, which also outlined the eligibility criteria for participants (C6). By offering a financial reward, Bitget aims to expand the pool of resources working on the recovery effort (C5).

The stolen assets were traced to wallets on multiple blockchains, including Ethereum, the XRP Ledger, Zcash and TRON, according to Bitget and blockchain‑intelligence firms (C7, C41). Users of Bitget are directly affected, as the $387.5 million loss represents a reduction in the value of their holdings (C2). The exchange’s containment claim indicates that further user funds remain at risk only if additional vulnerabilities are discovered (C8). Ongoing collaboration with Mandiant, SlowMist and the broader security community seeks to prevent similar breaches in the future (C5). The cross‑chain nature of the theft highlights the complexity of securing assets that move across diverse blockchain ecosystems (C7).

sections.heading: Binance breach affected $6.3 billion in assets on 29 October 2026
paragraphs: An attacker moved approximately $6.36 billion out of Binance wallets on ten blockchains starting at 20:05 UTC on 29 October 2026. The theft occurred within 20 minutes and is the largest crypto heist on record, surpassing the $1.5 billion Bybit hack of February 2025 according to Source S11. Binance suspended all withdrawals and deposits on Friday, 29 October 2026, to manage the incident. The breach affected an estimated $6.3 billion in assets, and the exchange stated it would cover all hacking losses. While Binance asserted that user funds are safe, Source S11 reports the company posted contradictory messages on X by stating both that funds are completely safe and that it would cover all losses.

Initial investigation points to a compromised laptop belonging to a DevOps engineer that gave the attacker access to a service container. This access enabled unauthorized withdrawals, and the attacker used an EIP-7702 delegation to turn a Binance hot wallet into a sweeper. The actor pre-signed 50 authorizations that were executed in a 20-minute burst, according to Source S13. Binance is now working with law-enforcement agencies, token issuers, and blockchain-intelligence firms to trace the stolen assets. The company stated it could freeze additional funds as it works with these partners, but Source S12 reports that Binance has not provided an update on the remaining $3.3 billion of assets.

Tether, Circle, Ripple, and World Liberty Financial froze approximately $2.67 billion in stablecoins following the breach. Arbitrum’s Security Council also froze 8,426 ETH and 74.6 million ARB, which totals approximately $2.7 billion. These actions resulted in approximately $3 billion, or about half of the stolen assets, being frozen on-chain according to Sources S11 and S12. Despite these freezes, the attacker still controls more than 420,000 ETH and 18,270 BTC, valued at about $2.4 billion. These specific assets are held in wallets that are beyond the reach of any issuer, according to the data provided in Source S13.

Bitcoin price fell over 4% after the announcement of the hack, and the asset dropped more than 3% to a six-week low according to Source S12. Ethereum price also fell more than 3% to a two-month low following the incident. These price drops affected broader crypto-market participants, while exchange users faced the direct loss of assets. The attacker laundered proceeds through large swaps with market makers and borrowing on Aave, which is a different pattern from the bridge-heavy laundering seen after the Bybit hack. This method of laundering involved using lending protocols to move the stolen funds, according to the analysis in Source S13.

TRM Labs attributes the Binance hack with high confidence to the TraderTraitor group, which is linked to North Korea’s Lazarus Group. The group is described as North Korea’s elite hacking unit in Source S13. These state-run crypto-theft programs provide funds for the weapons programs of the North Korean regime. The financial losses from these operations are borne by private users, exchanges, and the stability of the market. According to Source S8, the FBI reports that North Korean IT workers use stolen identities and threats of violence to fund nuclear and missile programs. This specific theft from Binance is the largest in history according to Source S13.

Bitget users also experienced a pause in withdrawals after the 24 September hack, but the exchange began restoring them in stages starting 28 September for BTC, according to source S1. ETH and related chains were restored on 29 September, followed by USDT on 30 September and other assets on 2 October, according to source S1. Bitget launched a bounty program to recover funds, paying 5 % of any frozen or recovered funds to individuals who assist, according to source S1.

North Korean regime officials are the beneficiaries of these thefts, which fund nuclear and missile programs, according to source S8. The FBI reports that North Korean IT workers use stolen identities and threats of violence to obtain payments, according to source S8. These workers pay Americans for services such as verifying identities and handling equipment to facilitate these schemes, according to source S8. Russian nationals Ilya Aleksandrovich Boykov and Vitold Viktorovich Obertas were sanctioned by OFAC for converting millions of dollars in cryptocurrency for North Korean IT-worker schemes, according to source S5. Boykov exchanged $3.5 million in cryptocurrency for front companies like Alis, which is a Vladivostok-based joint venture linked to Chinyong Information Technology Cooperation Company, according to source S7.

sections.heading: Binance and Bitget recovery efforts and unresolved asset losses
paragraphs: Binance has not provided an update on the remaining $3.3 billion of assets following the 29 October 2026 breach, although the exchange stated it will cover all hacking losses. Approximately $3 billion of the stolen assets have been frozen on-chain, and Binance said it could freeze additional funds as it works with partners. The company is currently working with law-enforcement agencies, token issuers, and blockchain-intelligence firms to trace the stolen assets. While Binance posted that user funds are completely safe, the exchange also stated it would cover all losses, which are contradictory messages according to source S11. These assets were moved out of Binance wallets on ten blockchains within 20 minutes starting at 20:05 UTC.

Tether, Circle, Ripple, and World Liberty Financial froze $2.67 billion in stablecoins, while the Arbitrum Security Council froze 8,426 ETH and 74.6 million ARB. These combined freezes total $2.7 billion, but the attacker still controls 420,000 ETH and 18,270 BTC, which equals $2.4 billion. These specific assets are held in wallets that are beyond the reach of any issuer, according to source S13. The attacker used large swaps through market makers and lending protocols for laundering, which is a different pattern from the bridge-heavy laundering seen after the Bybit hack. This method involved borrowing on Aave to move the funds. The total value of crypto stolen by North Korean actors in 2026 now exceeds $1 billion.

Bitget launched a bounty program that pays 5% of any frozen funds and 5% of any recovered funds to individuals who help freeze or recover them. Mandiant and SlowMist are assisting the exchange with the investigation into the 24 September hack. The stolen funds were traced to wallets on the Ethereum, XRP Ledger, Zcash, and TRON blockchains. Attackers used a cross-chain liquidity protocol for XRP instead of sending the assets to an exchange, according to source S4. Bitget says the hack is contained and no new thefts have occurred since the September incident. The exchange revised its loss estimate from $351.6 million to $387.5 million to include missed Zcash and TRON assets.

North Korean IT-worker schemes generate an estimated $250 million to $600 million in annual revenue for the DPRK regime, according to source S5. The FBI reports that these workers use stolen identities, extortion, and threats of violence to obtain payments that fund nuclear and missile programs. Some workers pay Americans for services such as appearing on camera or verifying identities to maintain these schemes. Russian national Ilya Aleksandrovich Boykov exchanged $3.5 million in cryptocurrency for front companies like Alis, which is a Vladivostok-based joint venture. Vitold Viktorovich Obertas converted $2 million in cryptocurrency and $1.25 million in other currency for North Korean officials since January 2025. These activities provide funds for weapons programs.

Exchange users and broader crypto-market participants bear the losses from these thefts, including those affected by price drops. Bitcoin fell more than 4% and Ethereum fell more than 3% in the hours after the Binance breach was announced. Bitget users are covered by its User Protection Fund, but Binance users may be at risk despite claims that their funds are safe. The Binance hack is the largest crypto heist on record, as it surpassed the $1.5 billion Bybit hack of February 2025. TRM Labs identified two primary Bitget-theft wallets that split stolen ETH into round-number wallets of roughly 10,000 ETH each. The laundering network used in the Bitget theft has not been seen working with any other group.
